fixes.explanation: Guard duty never comes up, friend. The enemies of Judah and Benjamin walk up to Zerubbabel, governor of Judah (Haggai 1:1), and say, “Let us build with you…” (Ezra 4:2). Their ask is a place on the building crew, not a spot beside the altar.

Cyrus king of Persia is the one, baker. Zerubbabel and the family heads say they must build “…as Cyrus king of Persia has commanded us.” (Ezra 4:3). They don't just say no. They name the king who gave the order. That's like turning someone down and pointing straight at the boss.

Belshazzar is a king from Daniel's book (Daniel 5:1), so I see why he came to mind. But he's in the wrong bakery, friend. The counselors keep going “…down to the reign of Darius king of Persia.” (Ezra 4:5). Cyrus and Darius are the two Persian kings the text names here.

Cyrus matters in this story (Ezra 4:3), so I get the guess, friend. But Rehum and Shimshai say “…that a search should be made of the record books of your fathers.” (Ezra 4:15). Old family records are what the letter names, not Cyrus's papers.

The king says, “It was discovered that this city has revolted against kings from ancient times, engaging in rebellion and sedition.” (Ezra 4:19). That's what came back after he issued a decree and a search was conducted. Then look what he builds on it: “…issue an order for these men to stop…” (Ezra 4:21). One report from the search, and the king is ready to give that order.
